notes:
Summary: Silverpine is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for real-time chat + reranking across two NA regions. Primary drivers: predictable tail latency for customer-facing conversational flows, deterministic cost per request, and strong audit/KMS controls for PII in scoring. They are risk-averse re: cold starts and want explicit reserved-GPU planning.

Key technical targets (customer stated):
- Target steady-state throughput: ~1,200 req/s for chat frontend (avg payload ~200 tokens).
- P95 latency goal: <150ms; P99 target: <450ms for 2k-4k context windows.
- Throughput SLO: 99.5% of requests under P95 target during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT).
- Burst handling: absorb 3x traffic spikes for up to 10 minutes without queueing to users.

Autoscaling / capacity concerns raised:
- Prefer a hybrid model: reserved baseline (4x A100-80G equiv) + autoscale up to 8 GPUs during peaks.
- Warm pool requirement: keep a pool of 2 pre-warmed nodes per region (warm containers + warmed KV caches) to avoid cold-start latency for chat sessions.
- Scale-up policy desired: proactive scale when queue length > 40 requests for 30s OR model token backlog > 50k tokens; reactive scale if p95 crosses 120ms for 60s.
- Scale-down policy: avoid immediate teardown; scale down only after idle < 120s and CPU/GPU utilization < 30% for 3 consecutive minutes to prevent oscillation.
- Queueing behavior: prefer bounded queue with graceful degradation (return short-form response or fallback model) instead of indefinite waiting. Max queue depth requested: 500 requests across region; overflow should trigger fallback to smaller quantized model or 429 with retry-after.

Model and infra preferences:
- Primary models: open-flan-like family quantized to 4-bit for reranking; for chat they want a 13B-70B class model with KV cache persisted to warm nodes.
- Kernel/quantization: need guidance from Redwood Optimize on q4_0 vs q5_0 tradeoffs given throughput/latency goals.

SLA / commercial negotiation notes:
- Silverpine Legal pushed back on blanket SLA credits; wants explicit p99 tail remedy and a short list of compensable failure modes (regional outage, cold-start > X, incorrect routing fallback).
- They asked for a documented warm-pool uptime guarantee and confirmation that reserved capacity will be physically isolated (no noisy neighbor).
- Pricing expectation: committed monthly reserved spend with overage at lower incremental cost vs hosted.

Conversation snippets (paraphrased):
- "We can tolerate isolated slow responses but not customer-facing timeouts during onboarding flows." (VP Product)
- "If the platform can guarantee 99.9% of p95 under 150ms, procurement is comfortable moving to commit." (Procurement lead)

Operational asks for POC:
- 2-week Dedicated POC in sa-east and us-west with simulated traffic (traffic script provided in drive link).
- Include telemetry template: per-route token breakdown, p95/p99 charts, queue-depth metrics, warm-pool hit-rate, and autoscale events.

Action items so far:
- Redwood to provide: detailed capacity plan mapping request patterns -> #GPUs, warm-pool sizing, and autoscale trigger fiche (Aisha owning).
- Legal to circulate draft SLA with p95/p99 definitions and remedies by 2026-03-18.
- Infra workshop scheduled: 2026-03-23 (workshop invite & agenda attached in drive).
